body.en: Start with a smile. In Swahili, 'habari' literally means 'news' (taarifa), so 'Habari gani?' is literally 'What is the news?' — in everyday use it means 'How are you?'. People usually answer with a feeling word such as 'nzuri' (good/fine). To give your name you say 'Jina langu ni …': 'jina' means name, 'langu' means my, and 'ni' is the little linking word meaning 'am/is'. After answering, ask 'Na wewe?' to mean 'And you?'.
body.sw: Anza kwa tabasamu. Katika Kiswahili, 'habari' humaanisha 'taarifa' au 'news'. Kwa hiyo 'Habari gani?' maana yake halisi ni 'Kuna habari gani?' — lakini kwa matumizi ya kila siku inamaanisha 'Ukoje?' (How are you?). Mtu kwa kawaida hujibu kwa neno linaloonyesha hali kama 'nzuri' (sawa, vizuri). Kusema jina lako sema 'Jina langu ni …': 'jina' ni neno lenyewe la jina, 'langu' humaanisha 'changu' (my), na 'ni' ni kijenzi kifupi cha kuunganisha kinachomaanisha 'am/is'. Baada ya kujibu, uliza 'Na wewe?' kumaanisha 'na wewe je?/and you?'.

phrases.en: How are you? (literally: what is the news?)

prompt.en: What does 'Habari gani?' mean?
prompt.sw: 'Habari gani?' maana yake ni nini?

options.en: How are you? / (literally) What is the news?

explanation.en: 'Habari' means 'news', so the phrase literally asks 'What is the news?' — a friendly way of asking how someone is.
explanation.sw: 'Habari' humaanisha 'taarifa/news', kwa hiyo maneno hayo yanauliza 'Kuna habari gani?' — namna ya kiungwana ya kuuliza hali ya mtu.

prompt.en: Someone says 'Nzuri, asante.' What did they most likely reply to?
prompt.sw: Mtu akasema 'Nzuri, asante.' Alijibu swali gani?

explanation.en: 'Nzuri' (fine) is the usual reply to the greeting 'Habari gani?'.
explanation.sw: 'Nzuri' (sawa/vizuri) ni jibu la kawaida kwa salamu 'Habari gani?'.

prompt.en: In 'Jina langu ni Emin', which word means 'my'?
prompt.sw: Katika 'Jina langu ni Emin', neno gani linamaanisha 'my/yangu'?

explanation.en: 'langu' means 'my'. 'jina' is the word for name, and 'ni' is the linking word meaning 'am/is'.
explanation.sw: 'langu' humaanisha 'changu' (my). 'jina' ni neno la jina (name), na 'ni' ni kijenzi cha kuunganisha kinachomaanisha 'am/is'.

body.en: Count: moja (1), mbili (2), tatu (3), nne (4), tano (5), sita (6), saba (7), nane (8), tisa (9), kumi (10). The numbers 1 to 5 can change their form to agree with a noun's class (e.g. 'vitabu vitano' = five books, 'vitano' matching 'vitabu'), but from 6 upward they stay the same. To say your age, use 'Nina miaka …' — literally 'I have (ten) years'.
body.sw: Hesabu: moja (1), mbili (2), tatu (3), nne (4), tano (5), sita (6), saba (7), nane (8), tisa (9), kumi (10). Namba 1 hadi 5 zinaweza kubadilika ili zilingane na ngeli ya nomino (k.m. 'vitabu vitano' = vitabu vitano, ambapo 'vitano' linalingana na ngeli ya 'vitabu'), lakini toka 6 na kuendelea hazibadiliki. Kuongelea umri wako, sema 'Nina miaka …' — humaanisha 'nina miaka kumi' (I am ten years old).

phrases.en: I am ten years old. (literally: I have ten years)

prompt.en: What number is 'tano'?
prompt.sw: 'Tano' ni namba ngapi?

explanation.en: 'tano' means five.
explanation.sw: 'tano' humaanisha tano (five).

prompt.en: What does 'Nina vitabu vitano' mean?
prompt.sw: 'Nina vitabu vitano' maana yake ni nini?

explanation.en: 'nina' = I have, 'vitabu' = books, 'vitano' = five (matching the noun class of 'vitabu').
explanation.sw: 'nina' = nina (I have), 'vitabu' = vitabu (books), 'vitano' = vitano vinavyolingana na ngeli ya 'vitabu'.

prompt.en: Which group of numbers never changes its form in Swahili?
prompt.sw: Ni kundi gani la namba lisilobadilika kwa Kiswahili?

explanation.en: From 6 upward the number words stay the same; only the set 1–5 can change to agree with the noun class.
explanation.sw: Namba 6 na zaidi hazibadiliki; ni namba 1–5 pekee zinazoweza kubadilika kufuata ngeli ya nomino.

sources.title: Noun Classes: the Cornerstone of Swahili Grammar (Swahili Grammar Guide)

body.en: Nouns for people use the m-/wa- class: the singular usually starts with 'm-' and the plural with 'wa-'. Examples: mtu → watu (person → people), mtoto → watoto (child → children), mwalimu → walimu (teacher → teachers), mwanafunzi → wanafunzi (student → students). Family words you can use every day: baba (father), mama (mother), kaka (brother), dada (sister).
body.sw: Majina ya watu hutumia ngeli ya m-/wa-: umoja kwa kawaida huanza na 'm-' na wingi na 'wa-'. Mifano: mtu → watu (mtu → watu), mtoto → watoto (mtoto → watoto), mwalimu → walimu (mwalimu → walimu), mwanafunzi → wanafunzi (mwanafunzi → wanafunzi). Maneno ya familia unayoweza kutumia kila siku: baba (baba), mama (mama), kaka (kaka), dada (dada).

prompt.en: What is the plural of 'mtu' (person)?
prompt.sw: Umoja 'mtu' — wingi wake ni nini?

explanation.en: People-nouns change 'm-' to 'wa-' for the plural: mtu → watu.
explanation.sw: Majina ya watu hubadilisha 'm-' kuwa 'wa-' kwa wingi: mtu → watu.

prompt.en: Which of these means 'mother'?
prompt.sw: Katika haya, neno gani linamaanisha 'mother/mama'?

explanation.en: 'mama' means mother; 'baba' is father, 'kaka' brother, 'dada' sister.
explanation.sw: 'mama' humaanisha mother/mama; 'baba' ni father/baba, 'kaka' ni brother/kaka, 'dada' ni sister/dada.

prompt.en: Which prefix makes a people-noun plural (e.g. mtoto → watoto)?
prompt.sw: Ni kiambishi gani kinachofanya neno la mtu kiwe wingi (k.m. mtoto → watoto)?

explanation.en: The 'wa-' prefix marks people in the plural (mtoto → watoto).
explanation.sw: 'wa-' ni kiambishi cha wingi kwa watu (mtoto → watoto).

sources.title: Noun Classes: the Cornerstone of Swahili Grammar (Swahili Grammar Guide)

body.en: A Swahili verb is built in a regular order: subject-prefix + tense-marker + verb-root. The subject prefixes for people are ni- (I), u- (you), a- (he/she), tu- (we; also m- for you all and wa- for they). The marker -na- points to the present: 'ninakula' = I am eating, 'unasoma' = you are reading, 'anakwenda' = he/she is going. The name 'Kiswahili' uses the ki- prefix that marks languages.
body.sw: Kitenzi cha Kiswahili hujengwa kwa utaratibu unaofanana: kiambishi cha nafsi + kiashiria cha wakati + shina la kitenzi. Viambishi vya nafsi kwa watu ni ni- (mimi), u- (wewe), a- (yeye), tu- (sisi; pia m- kwa ninyi na wa- kwa wao). Kiashiria -na- kinaonyesha wakati wa sasa: 'ninakula' = ninakula sasa hivi, 'unasoma' = wewe unasoma, 'anakwenda' = yeye anakwenda. Jina 'Kiswahili' linatumia kiambishi ki- kinachotumiwa kwa majina ya lugha.

phrases.en: He/She is going to the market.

prompt.en: What does 'unasoma' mean?
prompt.sw: 'Unasoma' maana yake ni nini?

explanation.en: 'u-' = you + '-na-' (present) + '-soma' (read): 'you are reading'.
explanation.sw: 'u-' = wewe + '-na-' (wakati sasa) + '-soma' (kusoma): 'wewe unasoma'.

prompt.en: In 'ninakula', what does the marker '-na-' show?
prompt.sw: Katika 'ninakula', '-na-' kinaonyesha nini?

explanation.en: '-na-' marks the present tense: something happening now.
explanation.sw: '-na-' ni kiashiria cha wakati wa sasa — kinachotendeka sasa hivi.

prompt.en: In 'tunakwenda nyumbani', the prefix 'tu-' means?
prompt.sw: Katika 'tunakwenda nyumbani', kiambishi 'tu-' kinamaanisha nini?

explanation.en: 'tu-' is the subject prefix for 'we', so 'tunakwenda' = we are going.
explanation.sw: 'tu-' ni kiambishi cha 'sisi', kwa hiyo 'tunakwenda' = sisi tunaenda.

sources.title: Noun Classes: the Cornerstone of Swahili Grammar (Swahili Grammar Guide)

body.en: Useful question words: 'nini?' (what), 'nani?' (who), 'wapi?' (where), 'lini?' (when), 'kwa nini?' (why), 'ngapi?' (how many). To ask 'What is this?' say 'Hii ni nini?' — 'hii' means 'this'. In Swahili a question word often comes at the end of the sentence, unlike English where it usually comes first.
body.sw: Maneno muhimu ya kuuliza maswali: 'nini?' (what/nini), 'nani?' (who/nani), 'wapi?' (where/wapi), 'lini?' (when/lini), 'kwa nini?' (why/kwa nini), 'ngapi?' (how many/ngapi). Kuuliza 'What is this?' sema 'Hii ni nini?' — 'hii' humaanisha 'this/hii'. Katika Kiswahili neno la swali mara nyingi huja mwishoni mwa sentensi, tofauti na Kiingereza ambapo linakuja mwanzoni.

prompt.en: What does 'wapi?' mean?
prompt.sw: 'Wapi?' maana yake ni nini?

explanation.en: 'wapi?' asks about a place or location: 'where?'.
explanation.sw: 'wapi?' ni swali la mahali: 'where?'.

prompt.en: 'Unaenda wapi?' asks about?
prompt.sw: 'Unaenda wapi?' linauliza kuhusu nini?

explanation.en: 'wapi' asks 'where', so the question asks where you are going.
explanation.sw: 'wapi' huuliza 'where/mahali', kwa hiyo swali ni unaenda wapi.

prompt.en: Which word means 'who?'?
prompt.sw: Neno gani linamaanisha 'who/nani?'?

explanation.en: 'nani?' asks about a person: 'who?'; 'nini' means 'what'.
explanation.sw: 'nani?' ni swali la mtu: 'who/nani?'; 'nini' humaanisha 'what/nini'.

title.sw: Maneno ya kila siku na utamaduni

body.en: These fixed phrases are everywhere in East Africa. 'Asante' means thank you; 'asante sana' = thank you very much. 'Karibu' welcomes someone (welcome / you're welcome). 'Hakuna matata' means 'no worries / no problem'. 'Pole' expresses sympathy when someone is hurt or tired; said twice, 'pole pole' means 'slowly'. Through centuries of coastal trade, Swahili also borrowed many words from Arabic and other Indian Ocean languages — 'asante' is one example.
body.sw: Maneno haya ya kawaida yameenea barani Afrika Mashariki. 'Asante' humaanisha 'thank you/ahsante'; 'asante sana' = 'thank you very much'. 'Karibu' humkaribisha mtu (welcome / you're welcome). 'Hakuna matata' humaanisha 'hakuna tatizo' (no worries / no problem). 'Pole' huonyesha huruma mtu anapoumwa au kuchoka; ikisemwa mara mbili, 'pole pole' humaanisha 'polepole/slowly'. Kwa karne nyingi za biashara ya pwani, Kiswahili kilikopa maneno mengi kutoka Kiarabu na lugha nyingine za Bahari ya Hindi — 'asante' ni mfano mmoja.

prompt.en: What does 'Hakuna matata' mean?
prompt.sw: 'Hakuna matata' maana yake ni nini?

explanation.en: 'hakuna' = there is no, 'matata' = problems; together 'no worries / no problem'.
explanation.sw: 'hakuna' = haipo (there is no), 'matata' = shida/matatizo; pamoja maana yake ni 'hakuna tatizo' (no worries).

prompt.en: Your friend is tired after work. Which word expresses sympathy?
prompt.sw: Rafiki yako amechoka baada ya kazi. Neno gani linaonyesha huruma?

explanation.en: 'Pole' is said out of sympathy when someone is hurt, tired or sad.
explanation.sw: 'Pole' husemwa kuonyesha huruma mtu anapoumwa, kuchoka au kuhuzunika.

prompt.en: When is 'Karibu' most often used?
prompt.sw: 'Karibu' hutumika lini hasa?

explanation.en: 'Karibu' welcomes a guest or says 'you're welcome'.
explanation.sw: 'Karibu' humkaribisha mgeni au kumjibu 'you're welcome'.

title.en: Your German path: from A1 to C2
title.sw: Njia yako ya Kijerumani: kutoka A1 hadi C2

body.en: German courses and exams are built on six levels of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR): A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2. A1–A2 are 'Basic User' (everyday phrases, introduce yourself, simple questions). B1–B2 are 'Independent User' (deal with everyday situations, explain opinions). C1–C2 are 'Proficient User' (use the language flexibly for academic and professional purposes). The Goethe-Institut offers a certificate exam at each level; A1 ('Start Deutsch 1') is the realistic goal for a beginner. These levels describe language ability only — they are not by themselves a residence permit or citizenship. A sensible path after A1 is A2 → B1 → B2 (living and working more independently), then C1 → C2 (academic and professional command), matching the 'can-do' descriptions at each step.
body.sw: Kozi na mitihani ya Kijerumani hujengwa kwenye viwango sita vya Common European Framework (CEFR): A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2. A1–A2 ni 'Mtumiaji wa Msingi' (maneno ya kila siku, kujitambulisha, maswali rahisi). B1–B2 ni 'Mtumiaji Aliyejitegemea' (kushughulikia mambo ya kila siku, kueleza maoni). C1–C2 ni 'Mtumiaji Mahiri' (kutumia lugha kwa ari kwa kazi za kitaaluma na kitaalamu). Goethe-Institut hutoa mtihani wa cheti kwa kila ngazi; A1 ('Start Deutsch 1') ndio lengo linalowezekana kwa mwanzilishi. Viwango hivi vinaeleza uwezo wa lugha tu — si kibali cha kukaa wala uraia wenyewe. Njia nzuri baada ya A1 ni A2 → B1 → B2 (kuishi na kufanya kazi kwa uhuru zaidi), kisha C1 → C2 (ufasaha wa kitaaluma), kufuatana na maelezo ya 'can-do' katika kila hatua.

prompt.en: How many language levels does the CEFR describe (A1–C2)?
prompt.sw: CEFR inaeleza viwango vingapi vya lugha (A1–C2)?

explanation.en: The CEFR groups proficiency into six levels: A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2.
explanation.sw: CEFR ina viwango sita: A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2.

prompt.en: Which two levels describe an 'Independent User'?
prompt.sw: Ni viwango vipi viwili vinavyoeleza 'Mtumiaji Aliyejitegemea/Independent User'?

explanation.en: C1–C2 are 'Proficient User'; A1–A2 are 'Basic User'. B1–B2 are the Independent User band.
explanation.sw: C1–C2 ni 'Mtumiaji Mahiri'; A1–A2 ni 'Mtumiaji wa Msingi'. B1–B2 ndio ngazi ya 'Mtumiaji Aliyejitegemea'.

prompt.en: Furaha is preparing for the A1 exam. What does A1 describe?
prompt.sw: Furaha anajiandaa mtihani wa A1. A1 inaeleza nini?

options.en: A proficient speaker of academic German
options.sw: Msemaji mahiri wa Kijerumani cha kitaaluma

explanation.en: A1 (Basic User) covers everyday expressions, introducing oneself and answering simple questions — exactly what Start Deutsch 1 tests.
explanation.sw: A1 (Mtumiaji wa Msingi) hujumuisha maneno ya kila siku, kujitambulisha na kujibu maswali rahisi — ndivyo Start Deutsch 1 inavyojaribu.

body.en: For centuries there was no single 'Germany' — instead, many German-speaking states and kingdoms existed. The German Empire was founded on 18 January 1871 after a series of wars led by Prussia, the strongest northern German state. Its king, Wilhelm I, became the Emperor (Kaiser), and Otto von Bismarck, the Prussian leader, became the first Chancellor. The empire lasted until 1918, when Germany became a republic after the First World War. Unification came through Prussian military power and diplomacy — not through everyone sharing one ethnic identity — and the new country stayed linguistically and culturally diverse, with many dialects and regional traditions continuing.
body.sw: Kwa karne nyingi hapakuwa na 'Ujerumani' moja — kulikuwa na majimbo na falme nyingi zenye kuzungumza Kijerumani. Dola la Ujerumani lilianzishwa tarehe 18 Januari 1871 baada ya msururu wa vita ulioongozwa na Prussia, jimbo lenye nguvu zaidi kaskazini mwa Ujerumani. Mfalme wake Wilhelm I akawa Kaizari (Emperor), na Otto von Bismarck, kiongozi wa Prussia, akawa Chansela wa kwanza. Dola hilo liliendelea hadi 1918, Ujerumani ilipokuwa jamhuri baada ya Vita Kuu ya Kwanza ya Dunia. Kuungana huko kulikuja kupitia nguvu ya kijeshi na diplomasia ya Prussia — si kwa kuwa watu wote walishiriki utambulisho mmoja wa kikabila — na nchi mpya ilibaki tofautitofauti kwa lugha na utamaduni, huku lahaja na mila za kikanda zikiendelea.

prompt.sw: Dola la Ujerumani lilianzishwa mwaka gani?

explanation.en: The German Empire was proclaimed on 18 January 1871, led by Prussia.
explanation.sw: Dola la Ujerumani lilitangazwa tarehe 18 Januari 1871 likiongozwa na Prussia.

prompt.en: Which German state led the unification?
prompt.sw: Ni jimbo gani la Ujerumani lililoongoza kuunganisha?

explanation.en: Prussia, the strongest northern German state, led the wars and diplomacy that created the empire.
explanation.sw: Prussia, jimbo lenye nguvu zaidi kaskazini, ndilo lililoongoza vita na diplomasia za kuunda dola.

prompt.en: Who became the empire's first Emperor (Kaiser)?
prompt.sw: Nani akawa Kaizari wa kwanza wa dola hilo?

explanation.en: Wilhelm I, King of Prussia, became Emperor; Bismarck was the first Chancellor.
explanation.sw: Wilhelm I, Mfalme wa Prussia, akawa Kaizari; Bismarck akawa Chansela wa kwanza.

title.en: How the German language took shape

body.en: German is a West Germanic language with many regional dialects. In the Middle Ages a northern 'Low German' and a southern 'High German' grew apart — the High German consonant shift (around the 6th century) marks their division. For a long time there was no single standard, and people from different regions often could not understand each other. Standard German emerged slowly as a written language, not from one place. A key step was Martin Luther's translation of the Bible into German (New Testament 1522, complete Bible 1534), based largely on the East Central German of the Saxon chancery. Helped by the printing press, this spread a common written form, and by the 18th century a widely accepted written standard had developed. Dialects still exist today alongside the standard language.
body.sw: Kijerumani ni lugha ya tawi la Kigermaniki Magharibi yenye lahaja nyingi. Katika Zama za Kati, 'Kijerumani cha Chini' (kaskazini) na 'Kijerumani cha Juu' (kusini) vilizidi kutofautiana — mabadiliko ya konsonanti za Kijerumani cha Juu (takriban karne ya 6) yanaashiria utengano huo. Kwa muda mrefu hapakuwa na kiwango kimoja, na watu wa mikoa tofauti mara nyingi hawakuelewana. Kijerumani sanifu kilijitengeneza polepole kama lugha ya maandishi, si kutoka eneo moja. Hatua kubwa ilikuwa tafsiri ya Biblia ya Martin Luther kwa Kijerumani (Agano Jipya 1522, Biblia kamili 1534), iliyotegemea zaidi Kijerumani cha kati-mashariki kinachotumika kwenye ofisi ya Saxony. Kwa msaada wa mashine ya uchapishaji, fomu hiyo ya maandishi ikaenea, na kufikia karne ya 18 kulikuwa na kiwango cha maandishi kilichokubalika kwa upana. Lahaja bado zinapatikana leo sambamba na lugha sanifu.

prompt.en: What did Martin Luther's Bible translation help to spread?
prompt.sw: Tafsiri ya Biblia ya Martin Luther ilisaidia kueneza nini?

options.en: A common written form of German
options.sw: Muundo mmoja wa maandishi ya Kijerumani

explanation.en: Luther's Bible, printed widely, helped spread and standardise German as a common written language.
explanation.sw: Biblia ya Luther iliyochapishwa sana ilisaidia kueneza na kusanifisha Kijerumani kama lugha moja ya maandishi.

prompt.en: Where did Standard German come from?
prompt.sw: Kijerumani sanifu kilianzia wapi?

options.en: It developed over centuries as a written standard used across regions
options.sw: Kilijitengeneza kwa karne nyingi kama kiwango cha maandishi kinachotumika katika mikoa mingi

options.en: One king invented it in a year
options.sw: Mfalme mmoja alikivumbua kwa mwaka mmoja

options.en: It is only the dialect of Berlin

explanation.en: Standard German emerged gradually as a written standard (helped by Luther's Bible), not as one region's dialect or a decree.
explanation.sw: Kijerumani sanifu kilijitokeza polepole kama kiwango cha maandishi (kusaidiana na Biblia ya Luther), si lahaja ya eneo moja wala amri.

prompt.en: The 'High German consonant shift' mainly distinguishes?
prompt.sw: 'Mabadiliko ya konsonanti za Kijerumani cha Juu' yanatofautisha nini?

options.sw: Kijerumani cha maandishi na cha mazungumzo
Kijerumani cha Juu (kusini) na cha Chini (kaskazini)

explanation.en: The consonant shift, around the 6th century, marks the dividing line between southern High German and northern Low German.
explanation.sw: Mabadiliko ya konsonanti, takriban karne ya 6, yanaashiria mpaka kati ya Kijerumani cha Juu (kusini) na cha Chini (kaskazini).

body.en: After the Second World War ended in 1945, Germany was occupied and divided into four zones controlled by the USA, Britain, France and the Soviet Union. As the Cold War deepened, two separate states were created in 1949: the Federal Republic of Germany (FRG, 'West Germany') — a parliamentary democracy — and the German Democratic Republic (GDR, 'East Germany'), whose politics were dominated by the Soviet-aligned Socialist Unity Party (SED). Berlin, deep inside the eastern zone, was itself split, and in 1961 the Berlin Wall was built around West Berlin to stop East Germans from leaving. This division was the result of war and Cold War politics, not of geography or ethnicity — Germans on both sides shared the same language and culture.
body.sw: Baada ya Vita Kuu ya Pili ya Dunia kumalizika mwaka 1945, Ujerumani iligawiwa katika kanda nne za udhibiti: Marekani, Uingereza, Ufaransa na Umoja wa Kisovieti. Vita vya Kiyu (Cold War) vilipoongezeka, dola mbili ziliundwa mwaka 1949: Jamhuri ya Shirikisho ya Ujerumani (FRG, 'Ujerumani Magharibi') — demokrasia ya bunge — na Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Ujerumani (GDR, 'Ujerumani Mashariki'), ambayo siasa zake zilitawaliwa na Chama cha SED kilichoungana na Umoja wa Kisovieti. Berlin, ikiwa ndani ya eneo la mashariki, nayo iligawanywa yenyewe, na mwaka 1961 Ukuta wa Berlin ukajengwa kuzunguka Berlin Magharibi kuwazuia Wajerumani wa Mashariki kutoka. Mgawanyiko huu ulitokana na vita na siasa za zama hizo, si jiografia wala kabila — Wajerumani pande zote mbili walishiriki lugha na utamaduni mmoja.

prompt.en: After WWII, Germany was divided into how many Allied occupation zones?
prompt.sw: Baada ya WWII, Ujerumani iligawanywa katika kanda ngapi za udhibiti wa Washirika?

explanation.en: Four zones: USA, Britain, France and the Soviet Union.
explanation.sw: Kanda nne: Marekani, Uingereza, Ufaransa na Umoja wa Kisovieti.

prompt.en: In what year was the Federal Republic (West Germany) founded?
prompt.sw: Jamhuri ya Shirikisho (Ujerumani Magharibi) ilianzishwa mwaka gani?

explanation.en: The FRG (West Germany) was established on 23 May 1949; the GDR (East Germany) on 7 October 1949.
explanation.sw: FRG (Magharibi) ilianzishwa 23 Mei 1949; GDR (Mashariki) 7 Oktoba 1949.

prompt.en: What kind of state was West Germany (the FRG)?
prompt.sw: Ujerumani Magharibi (FRG) ilikuwa dola la namna gani?

title.sw: Kuungana tena na demokrasia ya Ujerumani

body.en: The Peaceful Revolution in East Germany, with mass protests, led to the fall of the Berlin Wall on 9 November 1989, and Germany reunited on 3 October 1990 (now German Unity Day). Germany's democracy rests on the Basic Law (Grundgesetz), adopted in May 1949. It places fundamental rights in its very first articles and sets out the state's basic principles: democracy, the rule of law, federalism and the social state. Its institutions include the Bundestag (the directly elected parliament, whose members elect the Chancellor) and the Federal Constitutional Court, which is the guardian of the constitution. Since reunification, the elections and institutions that began in the West now cover the whole country.
body.sw: Mapinduzi ya Amani (Peaceful Revolution) mashariki mwa Ujerumani, pamoja na maandamano makubwa, yalisababisha kuanguka kwa Ukuta wa Berlin tarehe 9 Novemba 1989, na Ujerumani ikaungana tena tarehe 3 Oktoba 1990 (sasa ni Siku ya Umoja wa Ujerumani). Demokrasia ya Ujerumani inaegemea Sheria ya Msingi (Grundgesetz) iliyopitishwa Mei 1949. Inaweka haki za msingi katika vifungu vyake vya mwanzo na kubainisha kanuni kuu za dola: demokrasia, utawala wa sheria, muundo wa shirikisho na dola la kijamii. Taasisi zake ni pamoja na Bundestag (bunge lililochaguliwa moja kwa moja, ambalo wabunge wake humchagua Chansela) na Mahakama ya Kikatiba ya Shirikisho, ambayo ndiyo mlinzi wa katiba. Baada ya kuungana tena, uchaguzi na taasisi zilizoanza magharibi sasa zinagusa nchi nzima.

body.en: Kiswahili (Swahili) is a Bantu language of the Sabaki branch — it is not an 'Arabic' language. Its grammar and core vocabulary — the noun classes, the way verbs are built, and everyday words — are Bantu, inherited over a long history from Bantu-speaking peoples who lived along East Africa's coast. The first inhabitants of the Swahili Coast were Bantu-speaking Africans. Linguists find that the basic core vocabulary (everyday words like person, water, house) is overwhelmingly Bantu; loanwords from other languages form a smaller part of everyday speech. So Swahili did not begin as a mixture invented by foreign traders — it grew out of local Bantu speech and later borrowed selectively from the trading peoples it met.
body.sw: Kiswahili ni lugha ya Kibantu ya tawi la Sabaki — si lugha ya 'Kiarabu'. Sarufi yake na msamiati wa msingi — mfumo wa ngeli, ujenzi wa vitenzi, na maneno ya kila siku — ni wa Kibantu, uliorithiwa kwa historia ndefu kutoka watu wanaozungumza Kibantu walioishi kando ya pwani ya Afrika Mashariki. Wakaazi wa kwanza wa Pwani ya Waswahili walikuwa Waafrika wanaozungumza Kibantu. Wanaisimu wanaona kwamba msamiati wa msingi (maneno ya kila siku kama mtu, maji, nyumba) ni wa Kibantu kwa kiasi kikubwa; maneno yaliyokopwa kutoka lugha nyingine ni sehemu ndogo ya mazungumzo ya kila siku. Kwa hiyo Kiswahili hakikuanza kama mchanganyiko uliobuniwa na wafanyabiashara wa kigeni — kiliibuka kutoka lugha za Kibantu za pwani na baadaye kukopa maneno kwa makusudi kutoka kwa wafanyabiashara waliofika.

title.sw: Biashara ya pwani na maneno yaliyokopwa kutoka Kiarabu

body.en: The name 'Kiswahili' comes from an Arabic word meaning 'of the coasts' (from 'sawahil', the coasts), pointing to the East African coast. From the 8th century onward, Muslim traders — mostly Arabs — settled permanently on the coast, and later, in the 12th century, Persian 'Shirazi' settlers arrived. Through centuries of trade and settlement, Swahili borrowed many words from Arabic — especially in religion, trade, law and administration — and some from Persian, Portuguese and English. But these are loanwords: they sit on top of a Bantu grammar. In everyday core vocabulary the base words stay mostly Bantu, and borrowing came through trade and contact, not conquest. Swahili is therefore best described as a Bantu language enriched by coastal trade — not a half-Arabic language.
body.sw: Jina 'Kiswahili' linatokana na neno la Kiarabu linalomaanisha 'vya pwani' (kutoka 'sawahil', pwani), likirejelea Pwani ya Afrika Mashariki. Kuanzia karne ya 8, wafanyabiashara Waislamu — wengi wao Waarabu — walikaa kwa kudumu pwani, na baadaye, katika karne ya 12, wakaja walowezi 'Washirazi' kutoka Uajemi (Persia). Kupitia biashara na makazi ya karne nyingi, Kiswahili kilikopa maneno mengi kutoka Kiarabu — hasa katika dini, biashara, sheria na utawala — na machache kutoka Kiajemi, Kireno na Kiingereza. Lakini haya ni maneno ya kukopa: yamewekwa juu ya sarufi ya Kibantu. Katika msamiati wa msingi wa kila siku, maneno ya asili yanabaki ya Kibantu kwa kiasi kikubwa, na ukopaji ulitokana na biashara na mgusano, si ushindi. Basi Kiswahili ni lugha ya Kibantu iliyoboreshwa na biashara ya pwani — si lugha ya nusu-Kiarabu.

title.sw: Utamaduni wa Pwani na miji-jimbo ya Kiswahili

body.en: The Swahili Coast stretches along East Africa from Somalia in the north to Mozambique in the south. Its people are a mix of African and Indian Ocean peoples, and this region is not a single country but a coastal and island culture. From roughly the 11th to 15th centuries the coast flourished with independent trading city-states and 'stone towns', connected across the Indian Ocean — trading gold, ivory, pottery, silk and glass. The Swahili people shared a common language (Swahili) and, over the centuries, adopted Islam; the first mosques on the coast date from the 9th century, and today the vast majority of Swahili people are Sunni Muslims. Religion and culture spread mainly through trade and settlement, not conquest. Many of these towns still exist today inside modern nations.
body.sw: Pwani ya Waswahili inaanzia Somalia kaskazini hadi Mozambiki kusini. Watu wake ni mchanganyiko wa Waafrika na watu wa Bahari ya Hindi, na eneo hili si nchi moja bali utamaduni wa pwani na visiwa. Takriban karne ya 11 hadi 15, pwani ilistawi kwa miji-jimbo huru ya biashara na 'miji ya mawe', iliyounganishwa kupitia Bahari ya Hindi — ikifanya biashara ya dhahabu, pembe za ndovu, vyombo vya udongo, hariri na glasi. Waswahili walishiriki lugha moja (Kiswahili) na, kwa muda wa karne kadhaa, kukubali Uislamu; misikiti ya kwanza pwani ilianza karne ya 9, na leo wengi wa Waswahili ni Waislamu wa Suni. Dini na utamaduni vilienea hasa kupitia biashara na makazi, si ushindi. Miji mingi kati ya hii bado ipo leo ndani ya nchi za kisasa.

body.en: Swahili grew from a coastal trading language into a shared lingua franca — a common language used by people of many different mother tongues. In the 20th century it gained a new role: after Tanganyika's independence in 1961, its leaders deliberately promoted Swahili to help unite a new nation of many ethnic groups. Today Swahili is a national or official language in several countries, including Tanzania and Kenya (Kenya made it a national and official language in 2010, and Uganda made it an official language in 2022), a national language of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and a working/official language of the African Union and the East African Community. It is spoken across East Africa and the African Great Lakes by more than 100 million people by many estimates, most of them as a second language. It is a shared regional language across many countries, not the voice of a single empire.
body.sw: Kiswahili kiliibuka kutoka lugha ya biashara ya pwani na kuwa lugha ya kawaida (lingua franca) — lugha moja inayotumiwa na watu wa lugha za mama tofautitofauti. Katika karne ya 20 kilipata nafasi mpya: baada ya uhuru wa Tanganyika mwaka 1961, viongozi wake waliendeleza Kiswahili kwa makusudi ili kuwaleta pamoja makabila mengi katika taifa jipya. Leo Kiswahili ni lugha ya taifa au rasmi katika nchi kadhaa, zikijumlisha Tanzania na Kenya (Kenya iliifanya iwe lugha ya taifa na rasmi mwaka 2010, na Uganda ikaifanya rasmi mwaka 2022), lugha ya taifa ya Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo, na lugha ya kazi/rasmi ya Umoja wa Afrika na Jumuiya ya Afrika Mashariki. Kinazungumzwa Afrika Mashariki na Maziwa Makuu ya Afrika na zaidi ya watu milioni 100 kwa makadirio mengi, wengi wao kama lugha ya pili. Ni lugha ya kikanda inayoshirikiwa na nchi nyingi, si sauti ya ufalme mmoja.
